elements.element: Renewal is either only by mutual written agreement or, if automatic, for successive 12-month terms.
elements.evidence: The clause uses the permitted automatic-renewal route and provides that each Service Option Attachment renews automatically for an additional term of 12 months.

elements.element: Customer may opt out of automatic renewal on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Either party, including Customer, may prevent renewal by written notice given at least 30 days before the current term ends.

elements.element: Vendor must remind Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: IBM is expressly required to notify Customer in writing of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the current term ends.

elements.element: Renewal-term price increases are capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause states that renewal charges may not increase by more than the lesser of the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index and 3%.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, the non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The clause requires notice at least 30 days before term end, which is within the fallback maximum of 60 days.

elements.element: Renewal-term price increases are capped at 5% or less.
elements.evidence: The lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap cannot exceed 3%, and therefore satisfies the 5% maximum.

result.reason: The redline implements the preferred automatic-renewal option: fixed 12-month renewals, a 30-day Customer opt-out, a 60-day IBM reminder, and the required CPI/3% price cap. It necessarily also satisfies the fallback. The changes are confined to renewal mechanics and pricing, while the surrounding term provisions remain operative. Drafting is clear overall, though “on at least 30 days' notice prior to” is slightly redundant.
